headline: Get Your Game On
intro: Get Your Game On uses game tasks to assess problem solving, design thinking, and programming-adjacent logic without relying on prior syntax knowledge.

hero.alt: Main screen of Get Your Game On
hero.caption: The assessment hub with seven tasks.

timeline.title: Visual programming task
timeline.shortText: Built a simplified visual scripting task that tests logic and debugging without requiring prior programming syntax.

media.alt: Visual programming task in Get Your Game On
media.caption: Nodes on the left control the playable character on the right.

annotations.label: Node palette
annotations.detail: Players assemble behavior from logic blocks inspired by Blueprint and Scratch.

annotations.label: Runtime
annotations.detail: The created script is evaluated rather than faked with a predefined solution.

annotations.label: Scoring
annotations.detail: Partial completion can be scored from observed behavior.

timeline.outcome: The task can distinguish logical progress even when the final solution is incomplete.

timeline.title: Report generation
timeline.shortText: At the end of the assessment, the game generates a PDF with metrics that can support course suitability decisions.

media.alt: Generated PDF report for Get Your Game On
media.caption: Generated assessment output.

annotations.label: Metrics
annotations.detail: Structured scores turn game actions into reviewable evidence.

annotations.label: Export
annotations.detail: The output is portable and can be reviewed outside the game.

timeline.outcome: The project connects playful interaction to a practical assessment workflow.

closing: This project is useful portfolio evidence because it combines interface design, game logic, scoring, and real-world stakeholder goals.
